'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli forces]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] recover the body of Nattapong Pinta, a [[Thailand|Thai]] national abducted by the [[Mujahideen Brigades]] during the [[October 7 attacks]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cev4l7kxdllo (BBC News)] 
**[[Israel]]i airstrikes kill 55 people in the Gaza Strip. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/israeli-military-retrieves-body-thai-hostage-gaza-defence-minister-says-2025-06-07/ (Reuters)]
**[[Israel]] announces that it killed Asaad Abu Sharia, leader of the [[Mujahideen Brigades]] which was responsible for the abductions of several hostages during the October 7 attacks, including [[Kidnapping and killing of the Bibas family|Shiri Bibas]] and her two young sons. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/heads-of-terror-group-that-abducted-and-murdered-bibas-family-killed-by-idf/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] air attack on [[Kharkiv]], [[Ukraine]], involving [[Shahed drones]], [[cruise missile]]s and [[glide bomb]]s kills four people and wounds at least 60 others, according to local officials. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-attack-ukraines-kharkiv-kills-three-wounds-22-mayor-says-2025-06-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Decommunization]]
**[[Kyrgyzstan]] takes down a 23-meter-tall statue of the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] leader [[Vladimir Lenin]], thought to be the tallest statue of Lenin in [[Central Asia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c201yy6gknpo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Six people are killed and two seriously injured after a gas cylinder exploded in [[Mardan District]], [[India]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1915978/6-dead-2-injured-as-gas-cylinder-explodes-in-mardan-officials (Dawn)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Assassination of Miguel Uribe Turbay]]
**[[Colombia]]n [[Senate of Colombia|senator]] and pre-candidate in the [[2026 Colombian presidential election|2026 presidential election]] [[Miguel Uribe Turbay]] is shot during a campaign event in [[Bogotá]], leaving him in serious condition. Police arrest a 15-year-old suspect at the scene. He died from his injuries while hospitalized two months later on August 11. [https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2025/06/07/atentado-miguel-uribe-turbay-capturaron-dos-presuntos-implicados-en-el-atentado-contra-el-precandidato-presidencial/ (Infobae)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/south-america/miguel-uribe-leader-colombian-right-opposition-shot-bogota-rcna211674 (NBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Prime Minister of Afghanistan|Afghan prime minister]] [[Hasan Akhund]] announces that no [[Afghan refugees]] who left the country after the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|fall of Kabul in 2021]] will be prosecuted if they return to [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2603723/world (Arab News)]
*[[2025 Latvian municipal elections|Municipal elections]] are held in [[Latvia]]. Preliminary results indicate the [[far-right]] [[populist]] party [[Latvia First]] leading with 18.2% of the votes, followed by the [[Centre-left politics|centre-left]] [[The Progressives (Latvia)|Progressives]] with 16.64% and the [[conservative]] [[National Alliance (Latvia)|National Alliance]] with 14.13% of the votes. [https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/news/latvian-municipal-elections-show-increasing-political-fragmentation/ (Euractiv)]

**In [[tennis]], [[Tennis in the United States|American]] player [[Coco Gauff]] defeats [[Belarus]]ian player [[Aryna Sabalenka]] 6<sup>5</sup>–7<sup>7</sup>, 6–2, 6–4 in the [[2025 French Open – Women's singles|women's singles final]] to win her first [[French Open]] title.
